spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Consider how far the wisdom that proceeded from the first wisdom in that state extended in a determinate degree: within that reception each distinct operation of truth remained in everlasting unanimity with the others. None of those operations stepped outside the command of order, nor violated the mutual trust by which each held the use committed to it, and this concord endured without end.

But falsity set against truth was already judged and overcome; for when disharmony arose it turned inward and was divided against itself. The whole dominion of that falsity fell into internal conflict; and even the derivative powers that had abandoned their deepest obscurities and risen to join it were judged, because disunion permeated them all. Thus that falsity was brought down and its allied persuasions were humbled, because the power of the first wisdom acts by the same law of order that also governs the lowest realm.

So long as the interior consociations bound up with that arcanum remain in agreement with that falsity, its dominion stands firm for a time: it is wondered at, it is credited with glory, it is treated as the honored one, and it exalts itself as though it surpassed and were more exalted than the opposing dominion that is about to break forth against it.

Yet the dominion sustained by that interior agreement is nonetheless compelled—by the order it abuses—to condemn the other dominion; and then its assumed eminence collapses. Those falsities are humbled and made subject to the governance of the truths established in opposition to them.

paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES: it establishes the stable, orderly unanimity of truths proceeding from first wisdom within a fixed degree of reception.
paragraph_translations.notes: The opening imperative and several damaged phrases resist certainty; “measure” is taken as a determinate degree of reception, and the mutual “command and order” is treated as use committed by good to truths.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Strong coherence: the chapter moves in a clear sequence—ordered unanimity of truths proceeding from first wisdom, the internal division and collapse of falsity, the temporary appearance of strength when supported inwardly, and the inevitable humiliation and subjection of falsity to opposing truth. The only stumble is a slightly abrupt comparative clause about the law governing the lowest realm, likely due to damage in the source wording, but it still integrates with the theme of order prevailing.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential teaching: unity/order is explained as a functional condition (agreement, measure, command/order) rather than as a ranked jurisdiction. No narrative break.
findings.evidence: Text: “in a [measure]… the greatness of the light with one another for ever… nor did one of them transgress the command and order that his brother had entrusted to him forever.” The spiritual reading’s story arises directly from function—“stable, orderly unanimity… within a fixed degree of reception,” and it notes only routine damage (“opening imperative and several damaged phrases resist certainty”) rather than a foreign layer intruding.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly correspondential, but with a localized seam/damage where a comparative clause is tacked on in a way that interrupts the logic. This is a genuine difficulty (awkward syntax/likely lacuna), not an administrative insertion.
findings.evidence: Text moves coherently through functional collapse-by-disunity: “because of the arising of disharmony it was divided within itself… the kingdom was divided… powers… left their abyss… were doomed because of the disunity.” The spiritual reading explicitly reports the only stumble here: “The line comparing how first wisdom functions is somewhat abrupt, likely due to textual damage.” That stumble corresponds to the clause: “because the p[ower] of that first light functions in the same way as the kingdom of this world.” This reads like an incomplete comparison (missing an explicating middle term), producing a rhetorical jolt without introducing governance lists or jurisdictions.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential continuation: temporary stability of the dark ‘kingdom’ is grounded in the functional condition of internal agreement (“associates in the mystery… in agreement”), not in named rulers/territorial administration. No sign of overlay.
findings.evidence: Text: “As long as its [associates in the m]ystery are in agreement with it, th[at] kingdom [stands firm]… it receives glory… surpasses… more exalted… other kingdom… about [to burst out] against [it].” The spiritual reading tracks this smoothly (“temporary stability… when supported by interior agreement”), and does not flag any non-participating names or jurisdictional catalogues—hallmarks of the administrative voice are absent.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential resolution: the humiliation/subjection follows as an intrinsic consequence of the same functional logic (agreement → temporary standing → compelled condemnation → subjection). No intrusive systematizing addendum.
findings.evidence: Text: “is compelled to condemn… and the[y] are humiliated and come under the hand of this kingdom that is set up against it.” The spiritual reading reports coherent closure (“completes the arc… inevitable humiliation and subjection”) and notes only “minor lacunae” that do not disrupt the narrative—again consistent with damage rather than later administrative layering.

textual_criticism.summary: 4 findings: the chapter is overwhelmingly clean correspondential substrate (¶2, ¶4, ¶5). The only stumble occurs in ¶3 at an abrupt comparative clause (“functions in the same way as the kingdom of this world”), best explained as local damage/elliptical syntax rather than administrative overlay. Recommendations: none for excision; none for annotation.
